| This variable is used to interpolate between variable values for technologies with and without CCS to represent achievement levels at some fraction between no CCS and the level specified in the CCS. For example, if the CCS technology represents an effectiveness of 90%, then the CCS Acheivement Fraction can be specifed at 0.5 to represent a system with average CCS effectiveness of 0.45. This fraction is entered as an association with the **CCS associated technology** (e.g., for the pair ``pp_coal`` and ``pp_coal_ccs``, it is entered in association with the ``pp_coal_ccs`` variable).
 | 
 | **NOTE**: this variable **does not** modify the prevalence (uptake) of CCS. It only modifies traits of CCS technologies, including the following variables:
* EmissionsActivityRatios (CCS reduces emissions per unit of input energy
* OutputActivityRatios (CCS reduces output per unit of energy due to on-site energy use increase)
* NemoMod Capital Cost (CCS generally increases costs)
* NemoMod Fixed Cost (CCS generally increases costs)

Additionally, population-level changes to diet impact the protein content of wastewater.

name: Land Use Yield Reallocation Factor
information:
The land use yield reallocation factor :math:`\eta \in [0, 1]` is used to represent land use responsiveness to changes in demands. 
 | 
 | If :math:`\eta = 1`, then **land use will be reallocated**, diverging from the specified transition matrix. If demands exceed carrying capacity to meet all livestock and crop demands, then the transitions into grassland and cropland are increased to meet demands. If the carrying capacity exceeds demand, then transitions to grassland and croplands are reduced (which also increases forested land). 
 | 
 | If :math:`\eta = 0`, then **land use will remain as specified**, and all remaining demands with be met with net imports. If the demand is less then carrying capacity, then there is an increase in net exports; if demand exceeds carrying capacity, there is an increase in net imports.
 | 
 | For :math:`\eta \in (0, 1)`, there is a mix of reallocation and net imports, which scales linearly between extremes.

name: Maximum Pasture Dry Matter Yield Factor
information:
| Maximum potential yield of pastures in tonne/ha/month. The number of grazing animals that pasture can support are bounded by the maximum potential yield. The number of AU (animal units) implied by carrying capacity cannot exceed this number.
 | 
 | Default maximum value taken from `FarmBrite <https://www.farmbrite.com/post/how-many-cows-can-i-keep-per-acre>`_ under the assumption of technically feasible maximum--excellent pasture with irrigation, or 6,900 lb/acre. Using a conversion of 907.1858189 short tonne per kg, we use 3.45 ston/acre => 3129.791075205 kg/acre. The, using 0.404686 ha/acre, we get 7733.875338422877 kg/ha, or 7.734 tonne/ha/month as a default maximum. This is approximateluy 92.81 when expanded to annual. 
 | 
 | **NOTE:** This number varies significantly by geography, climate, and pasture utilization rate, and users should take care to set it. In transformations, it can be increased by increasing the prevalenceo of irrigation in drier regions, though this increases water requirements for pastures significantly.

variable: Maximum Production Increase Fraction to Satisfy MinShareProduction Electricity
name: Maximum Production Increase Fraction to Satisfy MinShareProduction Electricity
information:
| Maximum increase in future electricity production--estimated as the fraction of estimated production total at **first last period :math:`= -999`. Set to 0 to stop new technologies from being constructed to increase  ``NemoMod MinShareProduction`` constraints.
